title: Crispy Chicken Spring Rolls with Shiitake and Cabbage
summary: Crisp fried wrappers hold a savoury chicken and vegetable filling, flavoured with shiitake, ginger and garlic and served with a sweet chilli dip.

ingredients.item: spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
finely shredded white cabbage and carrot

steps.title: Cook Chicken
steps.text: Cook the chicken mince in a non-stick frying pan on medium-high, breaking it up, until no longer pink and reaching 74°C, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Stir in the cabbage and carrot mix, shiitake mushrooms, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar and cook until the cabbage just softens, about 3 minutes, then off the heat stir in the sesame oil and spring onion greens, spread on a plate and chill for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Set a wrapper as a diamond, spoon a packed 80 ml of filling onto the lower half and shape into a log, then wet the edges with water, fold the bottom corner over, fold in the sides and roll up tightly to seal.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan on medium to 160°C and fry the rolls seam side down, turning, until golden, 2-4 minutes per side.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drain, cool for 5 minutes and serve with sweet chilli sauce.

tips: Make sure the chicken reaches 74°C before adding the other filling ingredients, so it's fully cooked.
Chill the filling before wrapping so it's firmer and easier to shape into neat rolls.
Keep rolled spring rolls under damp kitchen paper while you work, so the wrappers don't dry out and crack.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten freshly fried; leftovers keep in the fridge for up to a day and can be recrisped in a hot oven. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
